bills.title: Requirements for Firearms Dealers
bills.summary: HB26-1126 (Requirements for Firearms Dealers) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The act clarifies that a state permit to engage in the business of dealing in firearms (state permit) is required for a firearms dealer (dealer) to transfer firearms. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently signed into law.

bills.title: Law Enforcement National Electronic Tracing System & Share Program
bills.summary: HB26-1265 (Law Enforcement National Electronic Tracing System & Share Program) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The act requires each local law enforcement agency, on or before September 1, 2026, to register for the United States bureau of alcohol, tobacco, firearms, and explosives national electronic tracing system and transmit to the electronic tracing system information about each firearm it recovers or confiscates within 90 days after recovery or confiscation of a firearm, subject to certain exceptions. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently signed into law.

bills.title: Colorado Bureau of Investigation Firearms InstaCheck Unit Operating Hours
bills.summary: HB26-1302 (Colorado Bureau of Investigation Firearms InstaCheck Unit Operating Hours) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. In current law, the Colorado bureau of investigation (bureau) must remain open 12 hours a day, every calendar day except Christmas and Thanksgiving, to transmit requests for a background check to the national instant criminal background check system and search other databases. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently signed into law.

bills.title: Prohibit Three-Dimensional Printing Firearms & Components
bills.summary: HB26-1144 (Prohibit Three-Dimensional Printing Firearms & Components) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The act defines 3-dimensional printing to mean additive and subtractive manufacturing. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently signed into law.

bills.title: Expand List of Petitioners for Protection Order
bills.summary: SB26-004 (Expand List of Petitioners for Protection Order) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The act adds a co-responder who is part of a co-responder community response to the list of community members who may petition the court for an extreme risk protection order. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently signed into law.

bills.title: Procedures Related to Civil Asset Forfeiture
bills.summary: HB26-1250 (Procedures Related to Civil Asset Forfeiture) is a support bill that supports and protects Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The act clarifies an existing requirement for the criminal conviction of a property owner by requiring that one or more criminal charges be brought as a prerequisite to any nuisance abatement or forfeiture proceeding. From a 2A perspective, this legislation advances firearm freedoms. The bill is currently signed into law.

bills.title: Record Keeping & Regulation of Sale of Firearm Barrel
bills.summary: SB26-043 (Record Keeping & Regulation of Sale of Firearm Barrel) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill requires a firearm barrel to be sold or transferred in person by a federally licensed firearm dealer. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Modify School Security Grant Program
bills.summary: HB26-1321 (Modify School Security Grant Program) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill modifies the definition for an 'eligible nonprofit organization' that may receive a disbursement from the school security disbursement program. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Colorado Bureau of Investigation Access Federal Fingerprint Search Service
bills.summary: HB26-1108 (Colorado Bureau of Investigation Access Federal Fingerprint Search Service) is a oppose bill that threatens and undermines Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill authorizes the Colorado bureau of investigation to participate in the federal bureau of investigation's rap back service, which allows authorized agencies to receive notification of activity on individuals who have submitted to a fingerprint-based criminal history record check. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Ban Government Access Historical Location Information Database
bills.summary: SB26-070 (Ban Government Access Historical Location Information Database) is a support bill that supports and protects Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill prohibits a government entity from accessing a database that reveals an individual's or a vehicle's historical location information, subject to certain exceptions. From a 2A perspective, this legislation advances firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Ban Government Purchase of Personal Data from Third Party
bills.summary: HB26-1037 (Ban Government Purchase of Personal Data from Third Party) is a support bill that supports and protects Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill prohibits law enforcement and other government entities from purchasing, or otherwise obtaining for anything of value, certain personal data from third parties. From a 2A perspective, this legislation advances firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Constitutional Carry of Handgun
bills.summary: HB26-1212 (Constitutional Carry of Handgun) is a support bill that supports and protects Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill grants a person who is at least 18 years old and permitted to possess a handgun pursuant to federal and state law the same authority to carry a concealed handgun as a person who holds a permit to carry a concealed handgun (permit). From a 2A perspective, this legislation advances firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Right to Firearm Possession & Elimination of Extreme Risk Protection Orders
bills.summary: HB26-1072 (Right to Firearm Possession & Elimination of Extreme Risk Protection Orders) is a support bill that supports and protects Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill codifies an individual's right to own, possess, and use a firearm to the maximum extent permissible by the state and federal constitutions. From a 2A perspective, this legislation advances firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Second Amendment Protection Act
bills.summary: HB26-1021 (Second Amendment Protection Act) is a support bill that supports and protects Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill repeals various state laws related to firearms and other weapons. From a 2A perspective, this legislation advances firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Lobbyist Regulation
bills.summary: SB26-147 (Lobbyist Regulation) is a amend bill that modifies Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The act requires a volunteer lobbyist to register and file a registration statement attesting they are not being compensated. From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.

bills.title: Use of Surveillance Technology by Law Enforcement
bills.summary: SB26-071 (Use of Surveillance Technology by Law Enforcement) is a amend bill that modifies Second Amendment rights in Colorado. The bill establishes the "Surveillance Accountability and Freedom Ensured (SAFE) Act" (SAFE Act). From a 2A perspective, this legislation endangers firearm freedoms. The bill is currently dead.
